Maya is standing in a supermarket queue, holding a carton of milk.
And then, for no reason at all, her heart starts to race.
Her brain's alarm system has just fired. The same one built to save her from a tiger.
Adrenaline floods her body. Her heart pounds. Her breathing speeds up.
She breathes so fast that her fingers begin to tingle, and the room starts to feel unreal.
Maya is sure she's having a heart attack.
This is a panic attack: a real alarm, with no real danger.
And alarms run out of fuel.
Within about ten minutes, the wave peaks. Then, slowly, it passes.
Maya is still holding the milk.
If this keeps happening, it's worth talking to a doctor. Panic attacks are common, and very treatable.
